reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all 5 files and found them safe. The package is a standard AUR binary package that downloads Visual Studio Code Insiders from Microsoft's official domain (vscode.download.prss.microsoft.com) with pinned SHA-256 checksums for all architectures. The PKGBUILD contains no dangerous top-level code, the install script only prints informational messages, and the launcher script reads user-controlled config files to pass flags to the binary. The inconclusive verdicts from Reports 1 and 3 are due to tool errors (API failures and parsing errors), not actual security concerns. Since Report 2 completed a full review without errors and found no malicious behavior, the correct verdict is safe.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool errors, not security findings. Report 1 failed with an HTTP 400 error when reviewing the install script. Report 3 (advisory) had parsing errors for .gitignore and the launcher script. Report 2 successfully reviewed all files. The inconclusive results are artifacts of infrastructure failures, not evidence of risk.

learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parsing errors) should not trigger inconclusive verdicts when other models successfully complete the audit. The system should distinguish between 'could not complete audit' and 'audit completed with concerns'.
When one model completes a full review and others fail due to infrastructure errors, the successful review should carry decisive weight rather than being diluted by failed attempts.
Implement retry logic or fallback models when primary models encounter transient API errors to improve audit completion rates.
The audit tool should track and report tool errors separately from security findings to avoid conflating infrastructure failures with package safety concerns.
